chapters.title: Connected is not yet qualified
chapters.text: Survey the complete package: dies, joints, substrate and cooling must cooperate in a specified environment over time. Today’s route asks whether heat can escape, defects can be found and lifetime claims have evidence. These questions belong at the beginning of design, not only at final inspection.

chapters.title: Locate the heat sources
chapters.text: Visit each die and consider power distribution under different workloads. Equal total power can produce different temperatures when hotspots move. Cooling design needs spatial and time-dependent information; one average power number cannot represent every operating condition.

chapters.title: Interfaces resist heat flow
chapters.text: Travel upward from the die through interface material, lid and cooler. Thickness, contact quality and material properties can each restrict heat flow. A larger cooler alone may not solve the problem. Identify the limiting part of the path before changing the hardware.

chapters.title: Assembly changes the heat path
chapters.text: Separate lid and interface to examine uniform contact and material continuity. Thickness variation and voids can change thermal resistance, while mechanical attachment affects contact. This is an inspection framework, not a transferable prescription for clamping pressure or interface thickness on a real product.

chapters.title: Read the thermal network
chapters.text: The separated-layer view shows heat can split through the substrate and surrounding structures, not only move upward. A simplified thermal-resistance network helps early reasoning if its assumptions are stated. The animation has no temperature scale and cannot provide junction-temperature readings or product acceptance results.

chapters.title: Function and failure evidence
chapters.text: Follow a test signal and distinguish component tests, post-package electrical tests and system workloads. They expose different failures. When a result is unexpected, preserve conditions and symptoms before narrowing the cause to power, interconnect, temperature, logic or another subsystem.

chapters.title: Thermal cycles accumulate stress
chapters.text: Watch conceptual expansion and contraction as different materials load joints and interfaces repeatedly. Reliability concerns change over time and cycling, not merely successful power-on after assembly. Real test conditions must follow the use environment and applicable qualification requirements, never the timing of this illustration.

chapters.title: Cross-check different evidence
chapters.text: Combine images, electrical results, temperatures and failure locations. One image can suggest a problem without proving its cause. Compare model predictions with measurements and record error and uncertainty. Engineering conclusions should be supported by validated data rather than the apparent realism of a visualization.

chapters.title: Improve against a fair baseline
chapters.text: Compare package or cooling options under the same workload, environment and measurement method, then evaluate temperature, power, reliability and cost. Changing many conditions at once obscures causality. An attractive improvement curve must be traceable to an experiment that can be repeated.

chapters.title: Beauty in verifiable order
chapters.text: Rise to see requirements, heat paths, assembly quality, testing and reliability form a feedback loop. Advanced packaging is beautiful when data, power and heat have deliberate routes and conclusions have evidence. Carry this map back to any packaging technology and ask how the complete system is verified.
